skill.name: skill-creator
skill.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
skill.summary: Create, test, benchmark, improve, and package reusable AI skills.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, CSS, fixed local paths, and ordinary variable names. Confirmed risks include unsafe HTML generation, symlink-following file reads, inherited agent execution, and automatic termination of processes bound to the selected viewer port. Publication should wait until these high-impact paths are hardened.

remediation.issue: Generated review pages can execute crafted embedded content.
remediation.suggestion: Escape script-closing sequences during JSON embedding, apply context-specific HTML escaping, and replace dynamic innerHTML construction with DOM APIs.

remediation.issue: Review and packaging workflows follow symbolic links.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinks and verify every resolved file remains within the approved workspace or skill root before reading or archiving it.

remediation.issue: The viewer terminates every process listening on its requested port.
remediation.suggestion: Never kill unknown listeners automatically. Select a free port or require explicit confirmation after proving ownership of the existing process.

remediation.issue: Evaluation and optimization run untrusted prompts with broad process access.
remediation.suggestion: Use restricted tool permissions, an isolated working directory, an environment allowlist, and explicit confirmation before running third-party eval sets or skills.

remediation.issue: Temporary report names can be predicted in a shared directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create reports with secure tempfile APIs and exclusive creation, then open the returned path.

remediation.issue: Local reports load fonts and executable code from third-party hosts.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle required assets locally or clearly disclose outbound requests. Keep integrity metadata pinned for any unavoidable external script.

semantic_findings.title: Generated Viewer Script Injection
semantic_findings.description: Untrusted prompts and output text are serialized into an inline script without escaping HTML closing tags. Crafted content can execute when the review page opens.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: json.dumps preserves less-than characters, and the result is inserted directly inside a script element. A closing script tag in embedded data breaks out reliably.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Eval Template Substitution

semantic_findings.title: Symlink-Following Output Embedding
semantic_findings.description: The review generator follows output symlinks and embeds the target bytes. A generated output can expose local files outside the workspace.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.is_file and the subsequent read methods follow symbolic links. No resolved-path containment or symlink rejection is present.

semantic_findings.title: Symlink-Following Skill Packaging
semantic_findings.description: The packager follows file symlinks during recursive collection. A crafted skill can include readable local files from outside its directory in the archive.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.is_file follows symlinks and zipfile.write reads the target content. The loop does not reject symlinks or enforce resolved-path containment.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Eval Prompts Run With Agent Access
semantic_findings.description: Raw evaluation queries are executed by Claude in the project root with inherited environment variables. Hostile eval data can induce unintended tool actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The query is passed directly to claude -p, and the process runs before trigger detection can stop it. No restricted tool policy or environment allowlist is supplied.

content.value_statement: AI skills can be difficult to design, test, and improve consistently. This toolkit guides creation, evaluation, benchmarking, review, and packaging across Claude and Codex workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates or revises SKILL.md instructions from user goals and examples.
Designs realistic evaluation prompts and objective assertions.
Compares skill-enabled outputs against baselines through repeated test runs.
Aggregates pass rates, timing, token use, variance, and configuration deltas.
Generates browser review pages for outputs, grades, benchmarks, and feedback.
Optimizes skill descriptions and packages validated skill folders as .skill archives.
limitations: Description optimization requires the claude CLI and active Claude Code authentication.
Automated evaluations can run many AI subprocesses and consume significant time and model usage.
Browser review requires a display or static HTML workflow; feedback handling differs in headless environments.
Packaging validates basic metadata but does not verify script safety, dependencies, or archive contents.

use_cases.title: Create a First Skill
use_cases.description: Turn a repeatable workflow into a structured skill with clear triggers, instructions, resources, and test cases.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Compare revised outputs with a baseline, collect human feedback, and refine instructions across measured iterations.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Skill Quality
use_cases.description: Measure pass rates, timing, token use, variance, and trigger accuracy before selecting a version.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill for [task]. Ask me about triggers, inputs, outputs, dependencies, and success criteria before drafting the skill.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the skill at [path]. Identify unclear instructions, missing resources, and repeated work, then revise it while preserving its name.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Against a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the skill at [path] with three realistic tasks. Compare skill and baseline outputs, define objective assertions, and generate the review viewer.

prompt_templates.title: Benchmark Two Versions
prompt_templates.prompt: Benchmark two skill versions at [paths] across [test set]. Analyze quality, variance, time, and tokens, then recommend and validate the stronger version.

output_examples.input: Create a skill that standardizes weekly incident summaries from notes and logs.
output: A concise SKILL.md with trigger guidance and a repeatable summary workflow.
Three realistic evaluation tasks covering complete, incomplete, and conflicting incident data.
Objective checks for chronology, impact, actions, owners, and unresolved risks.

output_examples.input: Test whether the revised spreadsheet skill performs better than the current version.
output: Parallel results for revised and baseline skill versions.
A benchmark comparing pass rate, execution time, token use, and variance.
A review page containing outputs, formal grades, and feedback controls.

output_examples.input: Improve this skill description because relevant requests do not trigger it reliably.
output_examples.output: A tested description selected using separate training and held-out evaluation queries, with before-and-after trigger scores.

best_practices: Define user intent, triggers, expected outputs, dependencies, and success criteria before drafting.
Use realistic tasks, objective assertions, baselines, and human review for meaningful evaluation.
Preserve the original skill name and validate every revision before packaging.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize instructions for only a few familiar examples.
Do not treat file existence or superficial formatting as proof of task success.
Do not run untrusted evaluation prompts or package unreviewed files without isolation.

faq.question: Can this skill create a new skill from an idea?
faq.answer: Yes. It gathers requirements, drafts the skill, creates test cases, and supports iterative review.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It can preserve the original name, compare revisions with a baseline, and refine instructions from feedback.

faq.question: Does evaluation require subagents?
faq.answer: Rigorous parallel comparisons use subagents. Claude.ai can run simpler sequential checks without baseline benchmarking.

faq.question: What does the review viewer show?
faq.answer: It shows prompts, generated files, prior outputs, formal grades, benchmark statistics, and feedback controls.

faq.question: What is required for description optimization?
faq.answer: It requires Python, the claude CLI, Claude Code authentication, and an approved set of trigger evaluation queries.

faq.question: Does packaging prove that a skill is secure?
faq.answer: No. Packaging checks basic structure and metadata, but authors must separately review scripts, dependencies, links, and bundled files.
